name: juvenile idiopathic arthritis overview
title: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis: fever with rash marks systemic JIA; otherwise the joint count in the first 6 months splits oligoarticular from polyarticular, and enthesitis or psoriasis marks the twins; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment in order, with uveitis screening and first steps below

root.title: Child with arthritis > 6 weeks, other causes excluded: which JIA subtype?
lines: onset < 16 · 1 or more joints · a CLINICAL diagnosis of exclusion
1 in 1000 children (rheumatoid arthritis 1% of adults) · the most common chronic rheumatic disease of childhood · mostly girls · rare before 6 months
inflammatory: morning stiffness, BETTER with movement, responds to NSAIDs · subacute or chronic · altered weight-bearing
screen with pGALS (gait, arms, legs, spine): joint or bone pain, fever + rash, limp, lost motor milestones, chronic disease with MSK links
red flags (constitutional, acute, severe or night pain, can't walk, red joint) → think of something else

head: h
Systemic (Still's disease)
10% · any age · boys = girls
the most SERIOUS subtype
pres: • peaks late afternoon to evening · well between spikes
• evanescent salmon rash with the fever
• aches WITHOUT swelling early, effusions later
• serositis · lethargy, weight loss, growth disturbance
case: 3 M, 3 months of fevers, faint rash for hours, pale, big spleen, knee + ankle effusions
inv: Often mistaken for infection or leukemia
tx: No fever → treat as oligo or poly

head: h
Oligoarticular
35% · girls 4:1 · under 6 (usually 1-3)
inv: soft tissue swelling, effusion, periarticular osteopenia · erosions UNCOMMON
tx: naproxen, indomethacin, piroxicam, meloxicam, diclofenac, celecoxib
Not improving or extends → poly course
⅓ remit · ⅓ stay ≤ 4 · ⅓ extend (extended oligoarthritis)

head: h
Polyarticular
girls 3:1 · peaks 2-5 and 10-14
insidious, ≥ 5 joints in 6 months · stiff ≥ 60 min · fatigue
rheumatoid factor (RF) splits it
pres: • POSITIVE 5% (3-5% of JIA): older, late teens, many joints, like adult rheumatoid arthritis
inv: case: 5 F, 3 months of knee swelling, morning limp · both knees, left wrist, many small hand joints

head: h
Enthesitis-related
10% · boys · over 10 (early teens) · often good prognosis
pres: • family history: ankylosing spondylitis, bowel disease, psoriasis, uveitis, reactive arthritis
painful red eye, photophobia, less vision · recurrent, may be both eyes

head: h
Psoriatic
10% · girls · BIPHASIC: young + preteen
inv: e.g. 8 F, oligoarthritis, family psoriasis, HLA-B27 +

panels.title: Uveitis: SILENT in oligo + poly, so SCREEN
items: risk: ANA +, girl, young, recent onset
slit lamp every 3 months if ANA + and onset ≤ 6 (first 4 years)
the most common extra-articular feature · first 4 years · does NOT follow the arthritis
complications: synechiae, glaucoma, cataract, band keratopathy, cystoid macular edema → BLINDNESS
treat: drops → oral steroids → methotrexate → infliximab or adalimumab

panels.title: Every new child: first steps
items: preliminary bloods SUPPORT, they do not diagnose: CBC (white cells, platelets ↑ in systemic; anemia) · ESR, CRP normal or ↑ · ANA = uveitis risk · RF (poly) · HLA-B27 (enthesitis-related)
team: physio, OT (assistive devices), nutrition, psychology, school · aims: comfort, function, no deformity, normal growth
refer to rheumatology AND ophthalmology or optometry

panels.title: Untreated synovitis: complications
items: muscle atrophy · contracture · joint narrowing, erosion, deformity · leg length difference
growth slows with active disease · early physis closure → short limb, small jaw (micrognathia) · inflamed in adolescence → LONG limb
ankylosis of neck, wrist · rarely joint replacement · lower school and work attainment
